title: Does this policy allow the request?

blocks.text: The trim planner's job role gets its own policy file, and the platform team wants each new policy checked in CI against the requests the job will make, and the ones it must never make. The lesson's `allows` knew only Allow statements written as lists. This one must handle what real policy files contain.
In `iam_check.py`, write `allowed(policy, action, resource)` for one identity policy document:

items: A statement **applies** when one of its `Action` patterns matches the action **and** one of its `Resource` patterns matches the resource. `Action` and `Resource` may each be a list of patterns or a single string (one pattern).

In a pattern, `*` matches any run of characters (also none) and `?` exactly one character; every other character matches only itself. Actions match in any letter case (`S3:getobject` is `s3:GetObject`); resources match case exactly.
The answer is `True` only if some applying statement has `"Effect": "Allow"` and none has `"Effect": "Deny"`. An explicit Deny always wins; with no applying statement, the request is denied.

blocks.text: This is a model of one policy, as the lesson's is: no conditions, no other policy types. The helper names `matches`, `as_list` and `applies` are declared for you; about 10 lines remain.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
from iam_check import allowed

BUCKET = "arn:aws:s3:::depot-plans-example"
policy = {
    "Statement": [
        {"Effect": "Allow", "Action": "s3:GetObject", "Resource": f"{BUCKET}/inputs/*"},
        {"Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["s3:PutObject"], "Resource": [f"{BUCKET}/plans/R-??/*"]},
        {"Effect": "Deny", "Action": "s3:Put*", "Resource": f"{BUCKET}/plans/R-00/*"},
    ],
}

print("GetObject inputs/day1.csv:", allowed(policy, "s3:GetObject", f"{BUCKET}/inputs/day1.csv"))
print("s3:getobject inputs/day1.csv:", allowed(policy, "s3:getobject", f"{BUCKET}/inputs/day1.csv"))
print("GetObject Inputs/day1.csv:", allowed(policy, "s3:GetObject", f"{BUCKET}/Inputs/day1.csv"))
print("PutObject plans/R-12/p.json:", allowed(policy, "s3:PutObject", f"{BUCKET}/plans/R-12/p.json"))
print("PutObject plans/R-123/p.json:", allowed(policy, "s3:PutObject", f"{BUCKET}/plans/R-123/p.json"))
print("PutObject plans/R-00/p.json:", allowed(policy, "s3:PutObject", f"{BUCKET}/plans/R-00/p.json"))

cases.says: the trim job's policy allows reading surveys and nothing it does not name
a Deny on a locked folder wins over the Allow that covers it
an Action or Resource written as one string is one pattern, not a list of characters
action names match in any case; resource names match case exactly
? in a pattern matches exactly one character
a pattern without a wildcard matches the whole name only, not a longer one that starts with it
